clue.text: I trained ref in sports

indicators.note: something trained has been worked into a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A self-taught referee boasting about training himself in various sports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like the speaker of the sentence, but it is the definition; the anagram fodder is all three words 'ref in sports'.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the pronoun I is the first-person singular form, so the grammatical term stands for it.

clue.text: Orators using similes and metaphors?

parts.note: orators are public figures known for their speech, and similes and metaphors are rhetorical devices; the phrase covers both readings

explanation.surface: A description of public speakers who lean on imagery in their speeches.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'figures' as people: speakers are figures of speech in a whimsical sense, while the usual sense names the similes and metaphors themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhetorical devices such as similes and metaphors are the standard examples of this term, and orators are jokingly the people of speech.

clue.text: Ill-tempered piper helped solve such a problem?

definitions.meaning: irritable and cross, in informal British usage

definitions.text: piper helped solve such a problem?
definitions.meaning: the Pied Piper of Hamelin cleared the town of its infestation of rodents

explanation.surface: A grumpy musician who nonetheless helped sort out some trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pied Piper legend: he lured Hamelin's rats away with his pipe, so the town's problem was a rodent one.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means irritable in British slang, and also describes a town overrun by rodents.

clue.text: Records attempt to produce work of art

parts.note: tapes are recordings
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Making recordings as an attempt at artistic creation.
explanation.definitionFit: A woven wall hanging is a traditional textile artwork, such as the Bayeux one.

clue.text: Use my pole when dancing

indicators.note: letters that are dancing move about, so the words my pole are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to make use of one's pole while performing a dance, as in pole dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something to use and to employ it are synonyms, both verbs.

clue.text: Game player in university staff room interrupted by noisy lot

indicators.note: the staff room abbreviation is broken into by the crowd, which sits inside it

parts.note: SCR is the senior common room, the staff room at a British university
a rabble is a noisy, disorderly crowd

explanation.surface: A games enthusiast in a university common room, disturbed by a rowdy crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: SCR, the senior common room, is the staff lounge at British universities.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone playing the word game Scrabble can be called a scrabbler, a player of that board game.

clue.text: London building redesigned again? Not really, with pounds needed for investment

indicators.note: a design reworked rearranges its parts, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A London landmark being redesigned once more, or perhaps not, with money required for the project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed for investment' tells you the L is put into the anagram mix of AGAINNOTREALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous art museum on Trafalgar Square is a celebrated London building.

clue.text: Light drink taken outside at end of evening, enjoying posh tent holiday?

indicators.note: the drink is placed around the light, enclosing it

parts.note: gin is a drink
a lamp is a light

indicators.note: the final letter of the word evening

explanation.surface: A lamp and a drink in the evening, on a luxurious tented holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamorous camping in luxury tents is the activity, so taking part in it is a posh tent holiday.

clue.text: Galatea's lover partly ostracised

indicators.note: only part of the word ostracised is used, a run of letters within it

explanation.surface: A mythical lover who was partly shunned.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Acis, a shepherd, was the lover of the sea-nymph Galatea, killed by the jealous Cyclops Polyphemus.
explanation.definitionFit: In Ovid's Metamorphoses the shepherd loved by the nymph Galatea bears this name.

clue.text: Appear pleased to start smoking

definitions.meaning: to ignite a cigarette or pipe

explanation.surface: Looking delighted at the prospect of taking up cigarettes.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to brighten visibly with joy and to ignite a cigarette.

clue.text: Film about one seaman recalled such as Captain Hook?

indicators.note: the film word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a film
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: called back, so the word for the sailor is turned around

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A film about a sailor remembered, featuring a character like Captain Hook.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Hook is a buccaneer in Peter Pan, so he is a sea-robber in character, the adjective's sense.

clue.text: Within a few weeks Republicans come together

indicators.note: the party letters sit inside the month

parts.note: May is a month, a stretch of a few weeks
R is the abbreviation for a Republican, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A political prediction that Republicans will unite within weeks.
explanation.definitionFit: To wed is to join together, the two partners becoming one.

clue.text: Winter footwear currently available in small chemists shop

indicators.note: the word for the present is found inside the shop pieces

parts.note: Boots is a British chain of chemists, or pharmacies
now means at present

explanation.surface: Winter footwear now on sale in a small branch of a chemist's.
explanation.walkthrough: Boots is the best-known British high-street pharmacy chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulated waterproof boots for cold weather and ice are footwear worn in winter.

clue.text: Not safe in botched rescue

indicators.note: a job botched is messed up, so the word rescue is jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone left in danger by a bungled rescue.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking security or protection means the same as being unprotected or at risk.

clue.text: In garlic we cultivated new kind of moth

indicators.note: as a garden plot is worked over, these letters are dug over into a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener reporting a new moth species found in their garlic crop.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearwings are a family of day-flying moths with transparent wings, often mimicking wasps.

clue.text: Star's key tune

parts.note: Alt is a key on a computer keyboard
an air is a tune

explanation.surface: A singer's signature melody, their key tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star's' means 'Star is': the 's links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The brightest star in the constellation Aquila bears this name.

clue.text: Frenchman drinks last of aged wine, getting plastered

indicators.note: the man takes in the letter, which goes inside him

parts.note: Rene is a French man's name

indicators.note: the final letter of the word aged

parts.note: red is a wine

explanation.surface: A Frenchman knocking back the dregs of old wine and getting drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastered' looks like slang for drunk, but here it is the builder's sense: a wall coated with plaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall given a coat of plaster or render is said to be rendered, a building trade sense.

clue.text: Lawless article revolutionary published? Cool

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: turning round, so the word for published is read backwards

parts.note: a paper ran a story, meaning it published it
chic means stylish, cool

explanation.surface: A lawless piece from a revolutionary being published, and considered cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like Che or a noun, but it is the signal to reverse RAN, giving NAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Without government or order, in the manner of anarchy, is a state of being without law.

clue.text: House needs extra rewiring at the front — electrician required

parts.note: gaff is British slang for a house or home

indicators.note: taking the opening letter of each of the words extra and rewiring

explanation.surface: A house needing additional rewiring calls for an electrician.
explanation.walkthrough: GAFF is British slang for someone's home.
explanation.definitionFit: On a film or TV set the chief lighting electrician holds this title.

clue.text: There's no information, doctor admitted, on a sex hormone

indicators.note: in an across clue, placed after the letter a
the doctor is let inside the other letters

parts.note: taken as written
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A doctor admitting there is no information available about a sex hormone.
explanation.definitionFit: Testosterone is the best-known example of this class of male sex hormones.

clue.text: Artist using restored frames

indicators.note: the words using restored surround the name, holding it inside like a picture frame

explanation.surface: An artist working with frames that have been restored.
explanation.walkthrough: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a French Neoclassical painter.
explanation.definitionFit: The French Neoclassical painter of La Grande Odalisque is a famous artist.

clue.text: Torn carpet sent back by business associate

indicators.note: placed beside the business abbreviation

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: returned, so the two words are read backwards

parts.note: rent means torn
to carpet someone is to rebuke them, to give them a rap

explanation.surface: A ripped carpet returned by a firm's partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns RENTRAP round, giving the second part.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner sharing in a firm or venture with others is a fellow associate.

clue.text: African country runs out of green vegetable

indicators.note: the letter for runs leaves the vegetable

parts.note: chard is a leafy green vegetable
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An African country running short of green vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: The landlocked nation in north-central Africa, capital N'Djamena, is the country named.

clue.text: Freely hang around with English writer

indicators.note: turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: hair or fabric that flows hangs loose and freely

explanation.surface: An English author loafing around without restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hang around' looks like loiter, but 'Freely hang' is one piece and 'around' turns it. The writer is the American Tom Wolfe.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Wolfe, author of The Bonfire of the Vanities, is a well-known American author.

clue.text: Unrestrained, outspoken author

indicators.note: spoken out, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: wild means without restraint

explanation.surface: An unrestrained writer who speaks his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar Wilde, the Irish playwright, was famous for outspoken wit.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Wilde, the Irish playwright and novelist of Dorian Gray, is a celebrated author.

clue.text: Studio more imposing in appearance? No way

indicators.note: the abbreviation for way is dropped from the longer word

parts.note: statelier means more grand and dignified in look
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A grander-looking studio, which the speaker denies outright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No way' looks like an exclamation of disbelief, but it tells you to remove ST.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's or designer's workshop is called by this French word, a workroom or studio.

clue.text: Greek ambassador repulsed European girl

parts.note: HE stands for His Excellency, the title of an ambassador

indicators.note: pushed back, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: Nell is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A Greek ambassador rejecting the advances of a European girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hellene is a native of Greece, the ancient Greeks' own name for themselves.

clue.text: After-school club showing film

definitions.meaning: whimsically, a club or society at a high school
the 1956 musical with Bing Crosby, Grace Kelly and Frank Sinatra

explanation.surface: An after-school club putting on a film screening.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the fashionable elite, and taken literally a society at a high school; it is also a 1956 musical film.
